iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_coverage_assessment:
Coverage is strong across all target fields:

• **cases_confirmed**: Multiple authoritative snapshots captured — 207 cases (Jan 29–Feb 28, MMWR mm7523a2), 325 cases (Jan 20–Mar 18, MMWR mm7520a1), 481 cases (as of Apr 4, DSHS second-death press release), 561 cases (as of Apr 15, Texas Children's), 800 US total with Texas as dominant contributor (Jan 1–Apr 17, MMWR mm7414a1). These provide a time-series of confirmed case milestones within the task window.

• **deaths**: Two Texas deaths within the task window are documented — DSHS Feb 26 press release (first death) and DSHS Apr 6 press release (second death, 481 cases as of Apr 4). Both DSHS press release URLs are now captured as discrete candidates (iter2_q1 surfaced the second-death page directly). The MMWR mm7520a1 confirms 1 death in the Jan 20–Mar 18 sub-period.

• **hospitalizations**: 60 hospitalizations (Jan 20–Mar 18, MMWR mm7520a1); 85 US hospitalizations as of Apr 17 (MMWR mm7414a1); 99+ hospitalizations referenced in Wikipedia (full outbreak arc, useful for upper bound). Texas Children's page (Apr 15) provides a hospital-level snapshot.

• **subnational_location / locality**: Gaines County, South Plains region, West Texas, Lubbock, Seminole (Reinlander Mennonite Church), Harris County all documented. SPPHD PDF (iter2) adds granular locality detail (Gaines County Ag Barn, mobile clinic locations).

• **date_reported**: Multiple dated milestones: Jan 29 (first case), Feb 26 (first death), Apr 4 (481 cases), Apr 6 (second death), Apr 7 (expanded counties health alert), Apr 15 (561 cases), Apr 17 (800 US cases).

• **source_url / source_type / evidence_quote**: All major source URLs are captured as candidates from authoritative domains (dshs.texas.gov, cdc.gov). Evidence quotes are available in snippets for all key data points.

• **cases_probable / cases_suspected / cases_unspecified**: Not explicitly broken out in available snippets; DSHS outbreak page (when fetched) may contain this breakdown. The MMWR reports use "confirmed" classification consistently. This minor gap is acceptable — the task window's confirmed case counts are well-documented.

• **Non-West-Texas cases**: Harris County (2 confirmed, Jan 2025) captured from iter1. The DSHS outbreak page references a "Cases Not Associated with the Outbreak in West Texas" section that will be accessible when the main outbreak page is fetched.
iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_trustworthiness_assessment:
Trust signals are strong:
- All primary case count and death data traces to dshs.texas.gov (official state health authority) and cdc.gov/mmwr (peer-reviewed federal surveillance reports).
- MMWR reports are authored by named CDC/DSHS investigators and carry standard epidemiological methodology disclosures.
- The DSHS second-death press release (Apr 6) is a discrete, dated official announcement — the highest-trust source for the second death within the task window.
- The SPPHD PDF is an official regional health district presentation, providing granular locality and timeline data with institutional authorship.
- News sources (Texas Tribune, NBC News, CIDRAP) consistently cite DSHS or CDC as their data source, making them acceptable corroborating sources for locality and hospitalization detail.
- Wikipedia is present but flagged as non-primary; it is useful only for contextual cross-checking.
- Facebook, YouTube results were surfaced but should be excluded from primary evidence — they are not authoritative sources for case counts.
- The DSHS Strategic Plan PDF and TSHAC meeting minutes (also surfaced) are not relevant to measles case data and should be excluded from the candidate set during downstream processing.
